newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.

text.p: The U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market remained at a standstill late Monday with owners pricing cattle at $66 to $67 per cwt and packers bidding $64, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of trade last week was at $64.

Dealers noted packers were under little immediate pressure to buy after making heavy purchases last week. USDA reported 133,500 head traded in Texas/west Oklahoma last week and said 103,700 head traded in Kansas.
"The bids are at $64 and that is not going to get it done," one Kansas dealer said.
Another Kansas dealer said that packers were unlikely to raise their bids on Tuesday with the two sides possibly finally coming together Wednesday.

"We sold them (packers) a lot of cattle last week and they are also only a week away from being able to draw on their August contracts," he said, noting packers appeared to be comfortable with their current inventory levels.
There were mixed reports of how quickly cattle purchased last week were being picked up, with some reporting a fast pace while others suggested the rate was just normal.
